title: Kodiak and IKEA to launch driverless freight operations in Texas
key_facts: Kodiak Robotics and IKEA Supply plan fully driverless freight in Texas later this year, with no safety driver in the cab.
IKEA is Kodiak’s launch customer for driver-out service.
Over four years Kodiak says it moved more than 1,300 IKEA loads and logged over 750,000 autonomous miles with a safety observer aboard.
First driverless service covers 219 miles, mainly along Interstate 45 between Houston- and Dallas-area Kodiak facilities.
The leg is part of a 292-mile route from IKEA’s Baytown distribution centre to its Frisco store.
Kodiak is still completing its highway safety case for driverless long-haul operations.
quote_evidence: The company is now completing its highway safety case for driverless long-haul operations.

Kodiak says focusing autonomous technology on long-haul highway routes could also allow human drivers to concentrate on local driving jobs while reducing the need for drivers to spend extended periods away from home.
why_it_matters_hint: First named customer for driver-out long-haul trucking in Texas, pending the safety case.
notes: All figures are Kodiak’s own, relayed by the outlet.
